children: Iron ore prices are higher in early Asian trade, supported by expectations for tighter port inventories and fluctuations in shipping costs, despite signs of weakening steel demand, say Chaos Ternary Futures analysts in a note.Global shipments have recovered, driven by increased volumes from Australia and nonmainstream suppliers, while Brazilian shipments declined, they say. Domestic port inventories fell, and iron concentrate production remained at a seasonal low, they add. Near term fundamentals show rising supply and softening demand, although lower inventories are providing some support, they say. The most actively traded January iron ore contract on the Dalian Commodity Exchange is 1.1% higher at 655 yuan a ton. (jiahui.huang@wsj.com; @ivy_jiahuihuang)
